evidence.claim: Putin proposed nominating Elvira Nabiullina for a third term in a bid to ensure macroeconomic stability, and Reuters noted she was a committed inflation fighter resisting pressure for rate cuts.
evidence.title: Putin tips central bank chief Nabiullina for third term to ensure economic stability
evidence.excerpt: Putin proposed nominating Elvira Nabiullina for a third term in a bid to ensure macroeconomic stability, and Reuters noted she was a committed inflation fighter resisting pressure for rate cuts.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters contemporaneous report based on a Kremlin spokesman and clear attribution of the nomination proposal.
evidence.period_fit: Target-year 2022; direct personnel decision during the sanctions shock.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct on the nomination proposal; partially indirect on monetary-policy empowerment because the central bank sets rates independently, but Putin's retention choice mattered.
contrary_evidence: The Bank of Russia still acted as an institution with some independence.
This says little about whether the broader economic agenda favored broad-based prosperity.

evidence.claim: Putin, his spokesman, and other Russian officials repeatedly denied that Russia planned to invade Ukraine; that denial was proved false when Russia launched a full-scale invasion on February 24, 2022.
evidence.title: Russian Rhetoric Ahead of Attack Against Ukraine: Deny, Deflect, Mislead
evidence.excerpt: Putin, his spokesman, and other Russian officials repeatedly denied that Russia planned to invade Ukraine; that denial was proved false when Russia launched a full-scale invasion on February 24, 2022.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: The article collates contemporaneous denials and directly checks them against the invasion outcome in the same week.
evidence.period_fit: Directly covers February 2022 statements and the target-year invasion.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Putin and his immediate public messaging, though the article groups him with other officials rather than isolating a single quote.
contrary_evidence: The piece does not provide a sworn admission by Putin; it shows the denial pattern and then the falsifying event.

evidence.claim: OFAC said Putin uses complex support networks to hide and move money and anonymously use luxury assets; it identified Graceful and Olympia as blocked property in which Putin has an interest and said Sergei Roldugin is a custodian of Putin’s offshore wealth.
evidence.title: U.S. Treasury Severs More Networks Providing Support for Putin and Russia’s Elites
evidence.excerpt: OFAC said Putin uses complex support networks to hide and move money and anonymously use luxury assets; it identified Graceful and Olympia as blocked property in which Putin has an interest and said Sergei Roldugin is a custodian of Putin’s offshore wealth.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: This is an official sanctions finding with named assets, named intermediaries, and explicit attribution language.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong official attribution, though the underlying ownership chain is intentionally opaque and the Kremlin denied the links.
contrary_evidence: The Kremlin denied affiliation with the assets; the precise beneficial-ownership chain remains partly hidden.

evidence.claim: HRW said Navalny’s March 22, 2022 conviction on new charges was a mockery of justice intended to silence him; the authorities also accused him of embezzling donations for personal gain.
evidence.title: Russia: Kremlin Targets Critics Amid Ukraine War
evidence.excerpt: HRW said Navalny’s March 22, 2022 conviction on new charges was a mockery of justice intended to silence him; the authorities also accused him of embezzling donations for personal gain.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous rights-monitoring report with explicit description of the prosecution’s political function and the contested embezzlement allegations.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strongly attributable to Putin’s government because the prosecution and sentence were carried out by state institutions under his rule, targeting his leading anti-corruption critic.
contrary_evidence: The embezzlement allegation is reported as the authorities’ claim and remains contested in the article.

evidence.claim: Navalny launched an international anti-corruption organization after his Russian Anti-Corruption Foundation was outlawed as extremist, and Reuters said his foundation had catalogued the wealth of senior Russian officials.
evidence.title: Russia's Navalny launches international anti-corruption fund
evidence.excerpt: Navalny launched an international anti-corruption organization after his Russian Anti-Corruption Foundation was outlawed as extremist, and Reuters said his foundation had catalogued the wealth of senior Russian officials.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters-syndicated reporting with a clear 2022 dateline; the article directly connects the anti-corruption crackdown to the outlawing of the foundation.
evidence.period_fit: Within 2022 and directly relevant to the treatment of anti-corruption scrutiny.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strongly attributable to the Putin system because the article says the court ruling outlawing ACF empowered authorities to jail activists and freeze accounts.
contrary_evidence: This is a report about Navalny’s response rather than a direct Putin quote or order.

evidence.claim: Authorities opened a new criminal case against Navalny for promoting terrorism and extremism, potentially more than doubling his sentence; Navalny said the existing convictions were trumped-up charges intended to silence him.
evidence.title: Russia's Navalny says he faces new criminal case for 'promoting terrorism'
evidence.excerpt: Authorities opened a new criminal case against Navalny for promoting terrorism and extremism, potentially more than doubling his sentence; Navalny said the existing convictions were trumped-up charges intended to silence him.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters report syndicated by Euronews with a 2022 dateline; the article gives the prosecution and Navalny’s response in the same piece.
evidence.period_fit: Target-year 2022, with the new case announced in October.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strongly attributable to Putin’s governing apparatus, though the article does not include an immediate official confirmation from investigators.
contrary_evidence: The article says there was no immediate official confirmation from the Investigative Committee.

unresolved_gaps: Direct evidence on command-and-control discipline, custody, accident-prevention, and other nuclear safety procedures in 2022 is thin.
Direct evidence on expert governance and risk institutions is weak relative to the rhetoric and escalation evidence.
The package needs better household and distribution evidence, not just macro stabilization and state-budget outcomes.
Direct evidence that appointments and institutions translated into durable productivity investment is still thin.
Direct 2022 delivery evidence for health, education, housing, and food security inside Russia remains thin.
Implementation and take-up by region and group are not well documented.
Direct documentary proof of Putin's personal beneficial ownership, asset control, or hidden conflicts remains limited.
The appointment and accountability map is still too thin for a fully rounded honesty judgment.
Direct 2022 implementation metrics for procurement, output, and battlefield effectiveness remain thin.
The package still needs a cleaner separation between frantic adaptation, temporary stabilization, and genuinely effective goal advancement.
